story.head: Minten has two goals as the Bruins take down the Sharks
paras: Charlie McAvoy played his first game of the season, after missing the first six. Fraser Minten opened the scoring for the Bruins midway through the first. Jacob Trouba scored his first goal for San Jose two and a half minutes later to tie it 1-1. McAvoy put the Bruins back ahead 2-1 a little over three minutes later. Ivar Stenberg, in his sixth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Macklin Celebrini, on the power play early in the second to tie it 2-2. Matthew Poitras restored the Bruins’ lead just under three minutes later, and Pavel Zacha made it 4-2 with just three seconds left in the period. Celebrini pulled the Sharks within one on the power play early in the third, but that was as close as they got. Darnell Nurse and Nikita Zadorov fought midway through the period. Minten scored his second of the night later in the period to make it 5-3 for the Bruins. Will Borgen scored his first goal for Boston into the empty net with less than two minutes left.

The Sharks outshot the Bruins 38-26, but the Bruins’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Jeremy Swayman made 35 saves for the Bruins, and Yaroslav Askarov allowed five goals on 25 shots. The Bruins moved to 5-2-0 and climbed into first in the Atlantic, while the Sharks dropped to 3-3-0, fifth in the Pacific.
